newsitem.title: DENMARK: OSCE offers to broker Serbia talks.
newsitem.headline: OSCE offers to broker Serbia talks.

text.p: The Organisation of Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) offered on Thursday to broker talks between the Serbian government and opposition to try to break a deadlock over last November's local election results.

Niels Helveg Petersen of Denmark said a meeting of the Swiss, Danish and Polish foreign ministers -- the so-called troika of past, present and future OSCE chairmen -- agreed on action to try to end the impasse.

"I have decided that we would start dialogue in Vienna, where the OSCE has its base, with representatives both of the Belgrade government and of opposition groups in order to explore all possibilities of making progress," he said.
"We will insist that the Belgrade government...accept the results of the municipal elections last November," the Danish foreign minister told a news conference after the meeting.

"We would at the same time enter into consultations with both opposition and government representatives at ambassadorial level in Vienna in order to see what we can we do to facilitate the democratic process in the former republic of Yugoslavia."
Petersen did not say if the offer had already been put to the two sides.

The Serbian government's decision to annul the victories of the Zajedno (Together) opposition coalition in local polls in Belgrade and 13 other cities sparked nine weeks of street protests and international condemnation.

The OSCE has sent observers to next Monday's elections in Chechnya and provided about $300,000 to pay for the polls, drawing criticism from Russian politicians who say the financing breaches Russian law against foreign funding of local elections.
Petersen, implying that the row had yet to be fully resolved, said that he was still in talks on the matter with Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov.
"I had this morning a discussion with Mr.Primakov. We discussed this issue and other issues and we are working to clear up any misunderstanding that might have occurred," he said.

"The basic issue really is that the OSCE is supporting these elections, supplying ballot boxes, communications and assistance in other technical areas of the conduct of elections the same as it has done elsewhere. There are no surprises here."
